title: High-Resolution Full-Chip Thermal Resistance Extraction of BEOL Interconnects in 3-D ICs Considering Detailed Via Connectivity
problem: Back-end-of-line (BEOL) interconnects play an important role in thermal dissipation in 3D ICs, but existing analytical models are inaccurate because they cannot consider detailed via connectivity.
motivation: To achieve accurate thermal resistance extraction for BEOL interconnects by explicitly modeling via connectivity for reliable hotspot prediction in 3D ICs.
method: Novel analytical model based on resistor network theory and the Woodbury formula that explicitly incorporates detailed via connectivity in thermal resistance calculations. Replaces previous approaches that ignored via-level connectivity details.
key_novelty: Resistor network model incorporating detailed via connectivity for BEOL thermal extraction in 3D ICs.
contributions: Analytical model using resistor network theory and Woodbury formula
Explicit modeling of detailed via connectivity in thermal calculations
3.4× improvement in accuracy compared with previous work
1.8% absolute percentage error in max temperature vs 5.2% previously
limitations: The model is specific to thermal analysis of BEOL interconnects and may require adaptation for other multi-physics simulations.
